title: What's your name?
canDo: say your name and ask someone's

dialogue.setting: It's Priya's first day at a new job in an office in Moncton, New Brunswick. The receptionist, Marie, greets her.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: Hello. My name is Priya Sharma.

lines.speaker: Marie
lines.en: Nice to meet you! I'm Marie.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: Oui. Priya, c'est mon prénom, et Sharma, c'est mon nom de famille.
lines.en: Yes. Priya is my first name, and Sharma is my last name.

lines.speaker: Marie
lines.fr: Merci. Ah, voici Luc. Luc, voici Priya.
lines.en: Thank you. Ah, here's Luc. Luc, this is Priya.

lines.speaker: Luc
lines.fr: Bonjour, Priya ! Je suis Luc, votre collègue. Bienvenue !
lines.en: Hello, Priya! I'm Luc, your coworker. Welcome!

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: Thank you, Luc. Nice to meet you!

vocabulary.note: Formal. Literally "How do you call yourself?"
A woman writes Enchantée. Both sound exactly the same.
Moi, je m'appelle Marie means "As for me, my name is Marie."
Formal. Without the rising voice, Vous êtes… means "You are…".
You'll see Prénom on every form.
On forms, Nom usually means your last name.
What you'll often hear at an office counter.
Used before some words, like mon prénom and mon nom. You'll learn the other forms later.
Use it to introduce someone or hand something over.
A woman coworker is une collègue.

grammar.title: je and vous
explanation: Je means "I". Before a vowel sound it shortens to j'. In this lesson you meet it in je m'appelle and je suis.
Vous means "you". It's the polite form for one person, and also the word for more than one person.
The verb changes with the person: je m'appelle but vous vous appelez, je suis but vous êtes. For now, learn these pairs as set phrases.

examples.fr: Je suis Luc. Vous êtes Marie ?

explanation: The French r is made at the back of the mouth, not with the tip of the tongue. Keep the tip of your tongue down, behind your lower front teeth.
Start from the g in "go", but don't close your throat completely: let the air rub through. It feels close to a light gargle.
Don't round your lips the way you do for an English r.

exercises.prompt: On a form, what do you write in the box marked « Prénom » ?
Someone says « Je m'appelle Luc. Enchanté ! ». What do you answer?

canDoCheck.prompt: At a clinic, the receptionist asks « Comment vous appelez-vous ? ». You answer:

canDoCheck.fr: Votre nom de famille, s'il vous plaît ?

canDoCheck.prompt: You want to know a new coworker's name. What do you ask?
